Hi Tom — thanks for the clear list. High-level options we support for Redwood Private (VPC or on-prem) — we'll tailor based on your security posture:

1) Push (recommended, minimal customer egress rules)
  - Syslog/CEF over TLS to a customer-managed collector (TLS, mutual TLS optional).
  - HTTPS JSON payloads to Splunk HEC (token-based).
  - OTLP/gRPC or OTLP/HTTP for traces to your OTEL collector.

2) Pull / Export (good for air-gapped setups)
  - Scheduled export of compressed logs/metrics to a customer S3-compatible bucket (server-side encryption with customer-managed KMS).
  - Periodic delivery manifests + object lifecycle for retention.

3) Sidecar/Collector (works inside VPC or on-prem)
  - Deploy Fluent Bit/Fluentd or an OTEL collector as a sidecar or node-level daemonset to transform and forward logs/traces.

Security & privacy notes:
- We mask any detected PII at the source if enabled; we can configure redaction rules or send raw logs to an internal collector for you to sanitize.
- Spans: trace IDs and span names include model and route info but we never emit raw prompt text by default. If you need full input-level tracing for debugging, we'll use an encrypted bucket with restricted keys and short retention.

Networking specifics (practical):
- If you want zero internet egress, we recommend VPC peering or PrivateLink to your collector endpoints and S3 VPC endpoints for exports.
- Minimum outbound ports: 443 (HTTPS, HEC, OTLP/HTTP), 4317 (OTLP/gRPC) and optionally 6514 or 514 for syslog/tls.
- IP ranges: for hosted fallback we publish ranges, but for private deployments you can avoid those by setting up routing to your collector.

I'll attach a Mapping Template (column: redwood_field -> splunk/cef/otlp) and an Observability Checklist for your compliance team. Also sharing our internal architecture diagram for private deployments here: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1aBcD-Private-Observability-Arch

- We can do a 30-min technical call to walk your SIEM team through a test export.

Let us know which option you prefer (Push via HEC / Syslog / OTLP OR Export to S3 OR Collector sidecar). If you prefer meeting times, we have availability Wednesday and Friday this week.

Adding a couple of engineering notes so the SIEM team has what they need: 
- OTLP payloads: we support both OTLP/gRPC (4317) and OTLP/HTTP (4318). We recommend gRPC for higher throughput.
- Trace sampling: default 1% for production; we can increase to a service-targeted 100% for short windows during debugging.
- Metric export: Prometheus exposition compatible metrics can be scraped by a Prometheus pull model if you run an internal scrape gateway, or we can push to a pushgateway-like endpoint.
- For Splunk HEC we recommend batching with at-least-once delivery and a small retry/backoff window.

I'll generate an example OTLP payload and a minimal Fluent Bit config for forwarding to Splunk (will drop into the Drive folder).

Markus
Senior Infra Engineer | Redwood Inference
